scope_notes: SetPt preview and committed commands share SetPointOptions.transform_at. PointTransform.SetPoint feeds the existing affine preview renderer. World constraints and destination-view CPlane constraints are covered independently.

Singular SetPt maps are admitted for preview only when the existing whole-object and selected-grip geometry editors accept the complete candidate batch. Invalid geometry holds the last valid preview, or displays only sources when no valid map exists.

Whole-object validation caches both success and failure by immutable geometry snapshot, affine map and tolerance across views. No display mesh is built for validation. Partial previews reuse the existing source/mode/index/map/tolerance/density cache.

The application retains frozen original source identities for Copy. Axis/alignment changes clear obsolete maps; Copy changes retain the map. Hover and preview updates preserve document geometry, both history stacks, saved preferences and the last accepted point.

Mouse hover and click resolve the same target. Prepared NURBS control/edit-grip geometry matches committed geometry through Copy and in-place edits in all four views and all three display modes. Independent tests exercise singular point maps, mixed-batch rejection, edit reconstruction overflow, CPlane changes and cache invalidation/pruning.

The explicit GPU readback matrix includes 12 SetPt point/mesh cases and 24 existing affine cases. These check selected target pixels, source style, face visibility, two color formats and cached GPU preparation reuse. This is implementation rendering evidence, not comparison against native Rhino mouse previews.

Full native SetPt grip/preview compatibility, performance, all geometry families, Solid/SubD grips and remaining grip behavior require further qualification. Live Rhino retesting was deferred because of the recorded Wine SSPI startup issue.
